Following the arrival of the Kota Cempaka last year, this achievement reflects our continued growth, our strategic investments in terminal infrastructure, and our unwavering commitment to operational excellence” ; emphasized that OMT’s ongoing modernization efforts, including the acquisition of additional state-of-the-art cranes, have significantly enhanced cargo-handling capabilities and reduced vessel turnaround time.

a4129.speaker: Jim Stewart, Chief Operating Officer of Onne Multipurpose Terminal (OMT)
a4129.speech: Noted the economic advantages of hosting such large vessels at Nigerian ports, explaining that direct calls by larger ships eliminate the need for transshipment via smaller feeder vessels — cutting down logistics costs and reducing freight tariffs for Nigerian importers and exporters: “This is not just a win for OMT; it’s a win for the Nigerian economy. The ability to berth larger vessels means more direct cargo movement, reduced logistics costs, and increased revenue for the country. Freight forwarders also benefit significantly, as they avoid the extra costs associated with transshipment.”

a4129.speaker: Yakubu Ezra, Chief Pilot of Onne Port
a4129.speech: Reaffirmed NPA’s technical readiness to handle large vessels: “At the Nigerian Ports Authority, we are fully equipped—both in training and technology—to safely pilot large vessels into our ports. The successful berthing of Kota Carum is evidence of our capacity and professionalism.”

a4184.speaker: Garba Hakimi, Colonel-Major (Doctor), Nigerien Minister of Public Health, Population and Social Affairs
a4184.speech: Indicated that this donation comes at a critical moment and “is testimony to an international solidarity for which we are deeply grateful.” He thanked UNICEF, on behalf of the Prime Minister, for its generosity and continued support. He said the kits distributed would offer essential assistance ranging from education to health and psychosocial support — all fundamental elements for the recovery and well-being of the affected families. He noted that the donation embodies a striking example of international solidarity and humanitarian commitment in that it constitutes immediate, quality assistance to those most affected, in particular children, who are often the most vulnerable in times of crisis. He extended particular thanks to all the members of UNICEF Niger and to all those around the world who contributed to this action.

a4184.speaker: Garba Hakimi, Colonel-Major (Doctor), Nigerien Minister of Public Health, Population and Social Affairs
a4184.speech: Committed to ensuring an efficient and equitable distribution of the donation, and promised to see to it personally that every kit reaches those who need it and that this aid is integrated into a comprehensive, coordinated response plan. “At a time when, for reasons of climate change, we are witnessing so many disasters all over the world, we must also remember that humanitarian aid is an important stage but that the road to reconstruction and lasting support is long,” he declared. He also invited all actors in the health system to reflect on their collective responsibility by continuing to work together to build a safer and more resilient future for the population. On behalf of the President of the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland, Head of State, he thanked all the technical and financial partners in health for the important support they have continued to provide to the health ministry, and UNICEF in particular for this donation.

a4184.speaker: Djanatou Mahondé, UNICEF Representative in Niger
a4184.speech: Stressed that this donation complements the support her institution already provides in the health sector in Niger, specifying that this support in Dosso comes in addition to the 11 billion CFA francs that UNICEF is investing in the health sector in support of the development programme in Niger. She reaffirmed UNICEF's commitment to remain alongside Niger in this constant effort to improve the health of the population, expressed her gratitude to all donors for their constant support, and finally thanked the government of Niger for the trust placed in her institution.

a4226.speaker: Bok Kang, Korean Ambassador in Mozambique
a4226.speech: Speaking to reporters on Friday in Maputo, said the aid will provide urgent relief to the internally displaced people in Cabo Delgado: “In addition to meeting immediate humanitarian needs, this support will also contribute to long-term solutions through regional development efforts, where part of this funding will strengthen the IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix, which helps to monitor displaced populations and improve response efforts” ; “We trust that the IOM will continue to be dedicated to its work, delivering significant results that will make a real difference to the lives of the people affected. Korea continues its commitment to supporting Mozambique, not only in humanitarian assistance, but also in the development of various projects, especially the construction of the Quelimane Central Hospital, the supply of essential medical equipment and training for health professionals”

a4226.speaker: Bok Kang, Korean Ambassador in Mozambique
a4226.speech: Believes that the collaboration between South Korea and IOM strengthens the collective capacity to meet the immediate and long-term needs of displaced communities in Mozambique.

a4226.speaker: Dinis Dinis, manager of the Shelter Programme in Cabo Delgado
a4226.speech: Explained that, in addition to Korea, the project relies on a variety of other donors, involved in rebuilding infrastructure and human dignity, which means that a large investment is needed in order to reach the largest number of displaced people ; “So far, needs have been identified in the districts of Mocímboa da Praia and Metuge”

a4262.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Lesotho's Trade Minister
a4262.speech: Said his government would send a delegation to Washington to argue against the new trade measure ; "My biggest concern was the immediate closure of factories and job losses," the AFP news agency quotes him as telling journalists on Thursday.

a4262.speaker: White House figures
a4262.speech: According to White House figures, in 2024 while the US exported just $2.8m (£2.1m) worth of goods to Lesotho, its imports from the southern African country amounted to $237.3m; US officials used the difference between the value of imports and exports in setting the tariff rates for different countries.

a4262.speaker: Teboho Kobeli, founder of Lesotho clothes manufacturer Afri-Expo Textiles
a4262.speech: "This has been a devastating day for us," told the BBC's Focus on Africa programme ; He said he had spent the day in talks with industry colleagues and the government about what to do next, and that while his business can look for other markets, the US is so significant that "we can't just shelve the US market... we need to do everything we can to bring [it] back."

a4262.speaker: Colette van der Ven, lawyer specialising in international trade
a4262.speech: Told the BBC that the 50% figure Trump has imposed on Lesotho "makes little sense logically"; she described it as "ironic" that the US was effectively punishing Lesotho for the success it has enjoyed under Agoa ; "It's this sense that the US is being taken advantage of because it's running a trade deficit. It's really reflective of a new ideology about trade and who is benefiting and who is not."

a4262.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4262.speech: Described the measures as "reciprocal tariffs" and said they were "for countries that treat us badly"; said that the US had been taken advantage of by "cheaters" and had been "pillaged" by foreigners ; "Our taxpayers have been ripped off for more than 50 years, but it is not going to happen any more" ; said the higher rates for the "worst offenders" were payback for unfair trade policies.

a4262.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4262.speech: "They have got some bad things going on in South Africa. You know, we are paying them billions of dollars, and we cut the funding because a lot of bad things are happening in South Africa."

a4262.speaker: South African presidency (statement)
a4262.speech: In a statement, condemned the new tariffs as "punitive", saying they could "serve as a barrier to trade and shared prosperity."

a4262.speaker: Parks Tau, South Africa's Trade Minister
a4262.speech: "We now have to look amongst ourselves and say, within the customs union in southern Africa... how we're going to respond to these issues" ; "Diversifying our trade is going to be important... enhancing our work on the African continent and collaborating," he is quoted by AFP as saying.

a4262.speaker: Annabel Bishop, chief economist at Investec
a4262.speech: Believes the impact will be "very negative", but told the BBC that the tariffs could accelerate the current shift in Africa's trading practices: "What we would expect to see is greater trade with the Global South, where possible, [there] is likely to be some switching in trade partners."

a4333.speaker: Khadija Mohamed Al-Makhzoumi, Somalia's Minister of Environment and Climate Change
a4333.speech: "Climate change is a matter of survival for Somalia." ; "The Climate Resilient Agriculture project, backed by the Green Climate Fund, will help over two million people restore our land, improve food security, and build resilience against the severe climate impacts we face today."

a4333.speaker: Green Climate Fund (GCF)
a4333.speech: Approved funding for two transformative projects valued at $134 million, to support adaptation and enhance the climate resilience of vulnerable agricultural communities in Somalia and Iraq; the announcements were made during the fortieth meeting of the GCF Board held in Songdo, Incheon, Republic of Korea from 21-24 October.

a4333.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
a4333.speech: "By empowering vulnerable communities with the knowledge, tools, and technologies needed to adapt, we are investing in agrifood solutions that bring food security, support livelihoods, and help countries confront climate change."

a4418.speaker: Andrea Tomaszewicz, Deputy Chief of Mission of the United States Embassy in Djibouti
a4418.speech: Stressed that “libraries symbolise hope for me… I am proud that the United States was able to cooperate with Djibouti to bring this project to fruition.”

a4418.speaker: Embassy of the United States in Djibouti (press release, cited as source)
a4418.speech: Said the United States inaugurated three new libraries in Djibouti benefiting the communities of Damerjog, Balbala and Ali Adde, built thanks to funding from the American people with the support of the Ministry of Education, local communities and Djiboutian companies; said the initiative strengthens the ongoing efforts of the American and Djiboutian governments to create education and employment opportunities for Djiboutian youth, and that the libraries received funding from the United States Africa Command under a US Department of Defense humanitarian assistance programme.

a4476.speaker: Fitch Ratings Agency
a4476.speech: Believes that the suspension of support from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) to Mozambique has contributed to the shortage of foreign currency (particularly of US dollars); according to a recent publication, USAID disbursements represented approximately three percent of Mozambique’s Gross Domestic Product “as a result of an investment, on average, between 250 million and 300 million dollars per year” ; “The Agency’s withdrawal not only left more than 2,500 people unemployed but also worsened the country’s economic situation, as its presence accounted for up to three per cent of the GDP. The shortage of foreign currency increased in 2025, in part due to the decline in external disbursements to the Government and the suspension of USAID.”

a4476.speaker: Fitch Ratings Agency (report)
a4476.speech: The country’s large financing needs pose a significant vulnerability although switch auctions on local-currency bonds, central bank borrowing, and short-term financing are being used to service debt: “The foreign exchange reserves have held up, but external disbursements have declined, which coupled with challenging domestic financing, increases risks of spillover to external repayments. Mozambique’s fiscal deficit widened to 4.9 per cent of GDP in 2024, from 2.1 per cent in 2023, mostly reflecting a decline in grants and some impact from the post-election violence on revenue collection.”

a4476.speaker: Fitch Ratings Agency
a4476.speech: Expects that the country’s fiscal deficit “will narrow to 3.4 per cent of GDP in 2025 and a forecast 3.6 per cent in 2026, mostly driven by falling expenditure. Financing constraints will contain capex, and we anticipate the public sector wage bill will fall relative to GDP. Nevertheless, budget rigidities will remain significant.”

a4476.speaker: Fitch Ratings Agency
a4476.speech: Says that the government accumulated, over the last year, external arrears to several bilateral and multilateral creditors (including the IMF, Portugal and the Islamic Development Bank): “In many instances, payments were only resolved after their specified grace period had elapsed. Fitch did not consider these incidents as defaults, as external commercial debt was not affected. Fitch understands that the accumulation of external arrears to the official sector has continued in 2025. The accumulation of arrears on domestic bonds also remains an issue, with the time for resolution of these delays having increased.”

a4494.speaker: President of ECOWAS
a4494.speech: According to the President of ECOWAS, Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso have got up to 29th January-29th July 2025 to remain within the ambit of ECOWAS.

a4494.speaker: Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso (governments)
a4494.speech: These countries have reaffirmed their commitment to break away or withdraw from ECOWAS and form their own sub-regional union, the Alliance of Sahel States.

a4494.speaker: H.E. Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a4494.speech: Articulated the suggestion of the Republic of Liberia at the just-ended 66th Summit of ECOWAS Heads of State and Governments that ECOWAS should remove all sanctions against the three countries and increase diplomatic efforts in negotiating with them in the spirit of international cooperation.

a4494.speaker: Kaydor (2024) (cited academic work)
a4494.speech: Cited for the claims that "there is a very strong connection between international cooperation and sustainable development" and that "international cooperation is the fulcrum for sustainable development", and that through international cooperation processes the ECOWAS region can ensure that mutually agreed outcomes are obtained in the ultimate interests of all member states.

a4689.speaker: Dovgalenko, Director of the Africa Partnership Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4689.speech: On the main lines of work of the new Africa partnership department: “Our task is to develop comprehensive relations with Africa, to make them genuinely strategic. Today it is a dynamic continent. It is not only a matter of enormous natural resources, the guarantee of African countries’ economic sovereignty, but of colossal human capital.”

a4689.speaker: Dovgalenko, Director of the Africa Partnership Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4689.speech: Said that in recent years Russian-African cooperation has been developing at a qualitatively new level, with a powerful impulse coming from the first and second Russia-Africa summits and the first ministerial conference of the Russia-Africa Partnership Forum held last November; said Russia is working with African friends on the practical implementation of the agreements concluded, supported by the Action Plan adopted at the St Petersburg summit, and that building relations with the African Union, regional and sub-regional groupings, alliances of states and multilateral formats is another key area of the department’s activity.

a4689.speaker: Dovgalenko, Director of the Africa Partnership Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4689.speech: On trade: said trade and economic cooperation reached a record $24.5 billion in 2023 and continues to grow, with work under way on major investment projects on the continent including in energy, the creation of transport and logistics chains, the formation of a secure settlement system, and high technology including space exploration and digital technologies.

a4689.speaker: Dovgalenko, Director of the Africa Partnership Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4689.speech: On the Alliance of Sahel States: said the creation of the “Alliance of Sahel States” Confederation is an important step in consolidating the efforts of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger to ensure national security and meet socio-economic challenges, that the association’s main objective is the fight against the terrorist threat in the Sahara-Sahel zone, and that the situation in the region is truly difficult, “including not without the help of the West, which participated directly in the destruction of the Libyan state in 2011”; said Russia helps both in strengthening counter-terrorism capacities and in reinforcing the combat capability of national armed forces by deploying military specialists and equipment, training military and law-enforcement personnel, and in the socio-economic development of the region’s countries.

a4689.speaker: Dovgalenko, Director of the Africa Partnership Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4689.speech: On food aid: said Russia provides humanitarian assistance to African populations in need through both bilateral channels and international organisations, with the UN World Food Programme a key multilateral channel; said the Russian government allocated the programme the necessary financing for the supply of national food products to Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger and Sudan, but that because of the sanctions imposed by Washington in November 2024 against Russian financial institutions, the transfer of funds has not yet been possible.

a4689.speaker: Dovgalenko, Director of the Africa Partnership Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a4689.speech: On education: said Russia gives priority to the training of highly qualified personnel among Africans called upon to ensure the economic and technological sovereignty of their countries, and that there are more than 34,000 African students in Russia, of whom about seven thousand are funded by the federal budget.

a4723.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a4723.speech: Expressed gratitude for Egypt's enduring support and collaboration, emphasizing their joint commitment to creating a prosperous and sustainable future ; underscored Somalia's cooperation with allies and international friends to safeguard the country's independence and unity ; "The Egyptian government and its people are longstanding allies and brothers who always work together for a bright future and sustainable development. Today's discussions demonstrate our commitment to strengthening diplomatic, security, and political relations."

a4723.speaker: Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, President of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a4723.speech: Extended appreciation to Egypt for its fraternal stance against Ethiopia's greed ambitions in the Somali Sea ; presented the economic and strategic importance of the Red Sea, and said that Somalia has a great share in this sea, which the government and its people do not accept that another country violates their rights.

a4723.speaker: Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, President of the Republic of Egypt
a4723.speech: Echoed concerns about the security, socio-economic, and political repercussions of Ethiopia's actions, emphasizing Egypt's solidarity with Somalia against any threat to its unity and territorial integrity ; cited the Arab League's mandate to jointly defend member countries facing existential threats ; "The law of the Arab League stipulates that we must jointly defend any Arab country that is facing an existential threat, so the Egyptian government does not accept any interference that violates the unity and security of Somalia. Egypt's power should not be tested by threatening its brothers, especially the brotherly countries that ask us to stand by them."

a4723.speaker: Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, President of the Republic of Egypt
a4723.speech: Praised President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on the significant achievements in Somali security, the fight against terrorism, and recent milestones such as the lifting of the arms embargo, debt relief, and integration into the East African Community.

a4829.speaker: Iran (government)
a4829.speech: According to Iran, ninety per cent of the targets were hit.

a4829.speaker: Ayatollah Khamenei, Iran's religious leader
a4829.speech: was heard to say that the missile bombardment carried out to avenge the blood of Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh and Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah, recently killed by the Israeli army, has been completed; warned that if Israel takes retaliatory action against Iran, Iran will unleash an attack worse than the previous one.

a4829.speaker: Ayatollah Khamenei, Iran's religious leader
a4829.speech: said in a speech at the end of the week that a large-scale war in the Middle East is inevitable.

a4829.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a4829.speech: answering a question from journalists at the White House, hinted that Israel would carry out a strike aimed at Iran's oil reserves rather than at its nuclear enrichment facilities.

a4829.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a4829.speech: said Israel is considering the retaliation it will take against Iran and that no decision has been reached; "The Israelis have a right to defend themselves. However, their military responses must be proportionate," he was heard to say in his exchange with journalists last Friday.

a4829.speaker: John Mearsheimer, scholar of international relations and politics
a4829.speech: says the conflict described as regional could include China, Russia and Iran as allies on one side, and North America and Israel, as well as the Western world, on the other; since the region is a large oil producer, the attention it attracts is correspondingly wide, describing the great strategic importance of the Middle East and the alignment of great powers into opposing camps; China, which has a high demand for oil, wants a significant share in the geopolitical balance of power in the Middle East; Russia is buying weapons from Iran for its war in Ukraine, including drones, while Iran obtains sophisticated air defences and jets from Russia.

a4829.speaker: John Mearsheimer, scholar of international relations and politics
a4829.speech: warns that the Houthis' attacks could become far worse, and gave his scholarly assessment that the Houthis will join the broad and full-blown Middle East war that is feared by carrying out similar attacks on Red Sea internet cables.

a4829.speaker: John Mearsheimer, scholar of international relations and politics
a4829.speech: says that even recently, 50 per cent of the missiles and rockets fired at Israel that failed did so through the US Navy; however, by military superiority alone, America and Israel cannot subdue their Middle East adversaries ; says it is impossible to destroy by military superiority the armed groups of countries lined up against Israel, noting that the heavy campaign Saudi Arabia waged against the Houthis years ago, coordinating 30 countries, strengthened the Houthis rather than destroying them.

a4829.speaker: John Mearsheimer, scholar of international relations and politics
a4829.speech: "Israel appears to be succeeding in widening the horizon of the conflict it began a year ago in Gaza and making it regional," and adds that no swift political settlement to the problem will be found ; says that of the four options - "establishing democracy in the land Israel holds through expansion, or accepting and implementing the Two State Solution, or else establishing an apartheid system, and worse than that, cleansing the land of Palestinians" - Israel has been implementing apartheid rule by preventing the first two from being carried out.

a4829.speaker: HGC, Hong Kong telecommunications service provider
a4829.speech: says the cables named Seacom, TGN, AAE-1 (Africa-Asia-Europe One) and EIG (Europe-India Gateway) were destroyed; said that as a result about 25 per cent of data traffic was disrupted and that the company provided a temporary solution by using other data-flow alternatives.

a4829.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's Prime Minister
a4829.speech: dismisses accusations of this kind; according to him, Israel is confronted by "monster" enemies but wants peace to prevail in the area, and has had the commitment to peace.

a4829.speaker: Ran Porat, researcher at the Australian Centre for Jewish Civilisation, Monash University
a4829.speech: says the feared Middle East war is on the verge of beginning and that Israel has stretched its forces ; "Although Hamas has been weakened and cannot do more than carry out guerrilla attacks, it has a certain measure of controlling power among Palestinian refugees. Therefore the war on the Gaza front is not over."

a4829.speaker: Head of the US military's Africa Command (AFRICOM)
a4829.speech: was recently heard to say that the Horn of Africa region has a very great chance of becoming a hatchery for the extremist groups al-Shabaab and ISIS more than at any other time.

a4949.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a4949.speech: Admitted concern about the possible closure of the US agency Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), with which Cabo Verde has a financing agreement, but rejected "lamentations" and indicated that he is looking for alternatives.

a4949.speaker: Various media outlets (cited)
a4949.speech: According to various media, the US government agency Millennium Challenge Corporation, which supports development projects above all in African countries including Portuguese-speaking ones, will suffer "significant reductions" in the number of staff and programmes, projected by Elon Musk's department.

a4949.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a4949.speech: Announced that the third Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) compact will prioritise connectivity and mobility in several dimensions - land, air, maritime, digital and human - an approach aimed at boosting the country's economic and social development.

a4949.speaker: President of Cabo Verde
a4949.speech: Indicated that Cabo Verde could be a reference point for hospital and pharmaceutical services in the region, as the country hopes to establish close cooperation with the United States, especially in the area of Health.

a4949.speaker: Delegation of the US Senate
a4949.speech: Classified Cabo Verde as a brilliant example of democracy in Africa, especially in view of the coups d'etat that have occurred in the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), of which the country is a member.

a4949.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde
a4949.speech: Announced that a delegation from the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) began a three-day visit to Cabo Verde to discuss the development of a new US funding package.

a5050.speaker: Onjezani Kenani, writer and social commentator
a5050.speech: Raised serious concerns about President Lazarus Chakwera's State House expenditure, questioning the moral and economic justification behind the administration's lavish spending; in a statement shared on social media he noted that during Peter Mutharika's tenure, the highest budget for the State House was $10 million ; “Akutani nazo ndalama za aMalawi abale?” Kenani asked in his native Chichewa, which translates to “What is he doing with Malawians' money, brothers and sisters?”

a5178.speaker: Temwa Msukwa, 12-year-old Standard Eight pupil at Kande Primary School
a5178.speech: Remembers how pupils and neighbouring communities would fight for the trickles from the only borehole that served up to 3 052 people, and says the intermittent water flow made it difficult for pupils to access water for everyday tasks such as drinking and cleaning their classrooms. “There was constant congestion at the borehole and people were often fighting for water. We rarely had enough clean water to drink and couldn't properly take care of our toilets and classrooms.”

a5178.speaker: Ministry of Health of Malawi
a5178.speech: Various diseases caused by gaps in access to safe water and sanitation account for over half of the outpatients in the country's hospitals, according to the Ministry of Health.

a5178.speaker: Sibongire Moyo, 14-year-old classmate of Temwa
a5178.speech: Says adequate clean water helps them take care of classrooms, toilets and surroundings.

a5178.speaker: Marshal Gerald Ngoma, Headteacher of Kande Primary School
a5178.speech: Says the new water system at the school is a great relief to the learners, teachers and the neighbourhood. He recalls classes frequently being disrupted as children spent more time fetching water from the overwhelmed borehole instead of learning. “It was hard to observe break time and that used to disturb teaching and learning. Children were scrambling for water at the only borehole we had and some were forced to fetch water from the stream.” ; Ngoma thanks Unicef and USAid for constructing the climate resilient water system that has eased access to safe water and created a safe learning environment for the learners and their teachers.

a5178.speaker: Alex Mwanjasi Mwakikunga, District community water supply officer
a5178.speech: Says Unicef has supported the construction of seven water points in Nkhata Bay with support from the US agency. “Most of them are located in health centres and schools, but they also meet the demand for safe water in surrounding communities.”

a5304.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5304.speech: On diplomatic relations: "Generally speaking, US interest in Africa remains minimal in relation to the stakes and expectations. Whatever the Americans choose, there should be no major revolution in US Africa policy, which has placed its priorities elsewhere since the end of the Cold War. However, one can expect more engagement from the Democrat Kamala Harris, who should remain in the same line as Joe Biden. During her Africa tour in March 2023, notably in Ghana, Zambia and Tanzania, the American vice-president said she was 'enthusiastic' about Africa's future and American-African cooperation. This contrasts with Donald Trump, if one considers his first term, during which his political interest in Africa was almost non-existent, even though in 2018 he launched his Prosper Africa economic initiative to strengthen trade with the continent."

a5304.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5304.speech: On trade and investment: "The most important will be AGOA, whose renewal must be decided in 2025. It should be noted that AGOA remains first and foremost a tool of coercive economic diplomacy (Economic Statecraft), since African countries that do not align with the American vision of human rights and democracy can be removed from it, as was the case with Rwanda in 2018 (under Trump) or Niger and Uganda in 2023. This policy should continue. Regarding investments, the 2022 US-Africa Summit restored American willingness to invest more in Africa, notably with the promise of $55 billion. Kamala Harris, who also announced support for digitalisation and innovation in Africa during her tour, should follow the same line. The United States also keeps an eye on Chinese expansion in Africa and wants to compete with Beijing in this sector, with investments in strategic infrastructure - such as American support for Angola's Lobito Corridor project. However, one can expect the same China-containment strategy from Donald Trump; competition with China on economic terrain is an obsession for the Republican, and his Prosper Africa initiative was to be placed in the framework of this competition with China and as a response to its Belt and Road Initiative."

a5304.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5304.speech: On security: "For the moment, this security dimension of American policy in Africa remains well relegated to the background in the American campaign. As stated above, Africa is not necessarily the priority question in this American electoral phase. But counter-terrorism still retains a certain importance for Washington. In this respect, the United States has particular worries regarding its military presence in the Sahel and competition from Russia. American troops were forced to leave Niger, where they had important military bases between Niamey and Agadez. Today, the challenge is to remain in the region. Cote d'Ivoire and Benin could host these troops, but in a West African climate increasingly hostile to Western military presence. Russia has above all gained legitimacy in this region with its presence now in Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, via its African Corps forces intended to place Wagner's forces under the Kremlin's wing. The new administration, whether under Trump or Harris, should have geopolitical responses to this new situation."

a5304.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a5304.speech: On development, humanitarian aid and governance: "Generally speaking, Trump, who pays less attention to Africa, should probably be less demanding on certain things, notably governance or human rights. Republicans are also less critical on these questions, even though Bush upended that. On the question of humanitarian aid, however, Trump, who has a mercantilist perception of international relations, had wanted to cut several funding streams intended for it during his first term. A subject that could come back to the table of Congress and call into question certain projects in Africa. The investments announced at the last US-Africa Summit to support the continent's development could also be revised by the Trump administration if he returns to power. However, where some Africans might prefer the Republican to Kamala Harris despite everything is on the LGBTQ question, which is contrary to our traditional and religious values. Kamala Harris, who says she is a great defender of this community, could tie American aid and investment more closely to the promotion or decriminalisation of homosexuality in African countries. On this question there is a fundamental civilisational divergence between Harris and several African countries, which will not exist with Trump, who is rather conservative and even anti-LGBTQ. As in the more critical or more 'paternalistic' tradition of the Democrats, Kamala Harris should be more demanding on questions of democracy and respect for human rights."

a5304.speaker: Kamala Harris, US Vice-President
a5304.speech: During her Africa tour in March 2023, notably in Ghana, Zambia and Tanzania, she said she was "enthusiastic" about Africa's future and American-African cooperation ; she also announced support for digitalisation and innovation in Africa during that tour.

a5347.speaker: Francois Venter, Professor and clinician researcher at Wits University
a5347.speech: Argues that "We're watching the largest HIV treatment programme in the world unravel in real time. We don't need perfection, but we need a combination of urgency, action, and strategy to save it" ; warns that "We are about to see a wave of new HIV infections, sickness, and death, with children born infected in record numbers. We will see our public hospitals further overwhelmed, and our hard-won victories against TB reversed. It is all preventable." ; "Sadly, Minister of Health Dr Aaron Motsoaledi and President Cyril Ramaphosa are charting their tragic legacy. This time, it isn't denialism; it's ignoring the problem." ; "While HIV programmes unravel and lives are lost, Ramaphosa and the government of national unity (GNU) are nowhere to be seen. Motsoaledi, once praised for his HIV leadership, offers no leadership, communication, or urgency." ; "It is difficult not to feel despair. I have seen the recent data on HIV testing, the PrEP numbers, the infant diagnostic stats, and, most shockingly, the viral load suppression figures, and they all paint the picture of a rapidly decaying system. I am seeing the consequences in Johannesburg's inner city, where I work." ; "We should have little patience for further delay and silence from our government. We cannot have a health department with no plan and, critically, no communication as to what is being done. Get the experts into the room, and get a plan together - with actual priorities, funding, targets, and partners. We don't need perfection, but we do need urgency." ; "The health system that is delivering HIV care is unravelling now. A combination of action, strategy, and urgency can save us. It will be hard. But the cost of doing nothing is millions of lives and a shattered legacy."

a5347.speaker: A study commissioned by the South African health department
a5347.speech: Suggests there will be between 56 000 and 65 000 additional deaths, and 150 000 new infections in just three years from the US withdrawal.

a5347.speaker: TB experts
a5347.speech: Predict 580 000 fewer people screened and 35 000 fewer people on TB treatment in 2025.

a5347.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a5347.speech: Estimates that health damage within Africa from the current funding cut is already, in just three months, the equivalent of 75% of Covid's peak damage.

a5347.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Minister of Health
a5347.speech: Announced a grand plan to get an additional 1.1 million people on treatment by the end of the year but with no operational plan, no reprioritisation, and no budget.

a5347.speaker: Senior university leadership (at a meeting of Wits University leaders)
a5347.speech: Told the author at a meeting to discuss the massive funding and job cuts that Ramaphosa, who appeared weekly on television during Covid, was "too busy with the G20" meeting to meet them.

a5347.speaker: Civil society's leading organisations
a5347.speech: Confirmed to the author that the president and ministers have not responded to formal letters asking for a plan, despite emails pleading with them to do so, beyond acknowledgements of receipt.

a5347.speaker: South African health department (press statement)
a5347.speech: Met the loss of hardworking NGO jobs not with concern, outrage, or even a word of thanks but with a hostile press statement; it also sent out a thin emergency circular that appears not to have been implemented at any level.

a5437.speaker: Molly Levinson, the players’ spokeswoman
a5437.speech: Said that they planned to appeal against the decision: “We are shocked and disappointed. We will not give up our hard work for equal pay. We are confident in our case and steadfast in our commitment to ensuring that girls and women who play this sport will not be valued as lesser just because of their gender.”

a5437.speaker: Federal judge Gary Klausner
a5437.speech: Allowed the players’ case for unfair treatment in travel, housing and medical support to go to trial, which is set for 16 June in Los Angeles.

a5437.speaker: The court (ruling)
a5437.speech: Giving its ruling, the court said: “The women’s team has been paid more on both a cumulative and an average per-game basis than the men’s team over the class period.”

a5437.speaker: Megan Rapinoe, US striker
a5437.speech: Tweeted after the equal pay claim was dismissed: “We will never stop fighting for equality.”

a5437.speaker: Alex Morgan, US striker
a5437.speech: “Although disappointing to hear this news, this will not discourage us in our fight for equality.”

a5437.speaker: US Soccer Federation (USSF)
a5437.speech: Said it wanted to work with the team to “chart a positive path forward to grow the game both here at home and around the world.”

a5437.speaker: US men’s national team (statement)
a5437.speech: Issued a statement in February criticizing the governing body, saying that “the federation continues to discriminate against the women in their wages and working conditions.”

a5498.speaker: Pre-webinar poll of attendees (conducted by the author, Olufemi Boyede)
a5498.speech: The results showed that 63% of attendees feel that exporting food will not worsen Nigeria's food crisis; for the second question, 56% of the participants said that some current government policies support food production.

a5535.speaker: Yakob Belay, Director of Road Safety Directorate at the Federal Transport Authority
a5535.speech: “We finalized the preparation of the database and the display board is being installed now.”

a5535.speaker: Yigzaw, Federal Transport Authority official
a5535.speech: “We chose to implement the directive on the commercial vehicles first is the nation is facing a tremendous threat with the alarmingly increasing deaths and loss of property year after year.” ; “Studies are showing 85% up to 90% of accidents occur due to speeding.”

a5535.speaker: Yigzaw, Federal Transport Authority official
a5535.speech: “We will call experienced importers to get licenses and import the machine starting from the week of the approval of the directive.”

a5535.speaker: Federal Transport Authority draft directive (document)
a5535.speech: Stipulates that the maximum speed will be 80kmh, unless a locality has put a lower speed limit into effect; any car made in 2000 or later will need to use ESG, with earlier model vehicles to be dealt with at a later date; the device will send the car’s data to a database using the telecommunication fleet management system, with the owner responsible for the costs.

a5535.speaker: Federal Transport Authority draft directive (document)
a5535.speech: Reads that drivers are obliged not to drive any vehicle which is supposed to have the speed limiter, and when there are problems with the machine they have to immediately stop the car and report the problem to the owner; the bill also states that anyone who sells the speed limiter should also have a trained team to install and maintain the machine, that shop owners are expected to carry only brands authorized by the authority and carrying any others will cause a penalty.

a5535.speaker: Studies (cited on road accidents)
a5535.speech: Studies are showing 85% up to 90% of accidents occur due to speeding.

a5572.speaker: Pierre Dimba, Minister of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Health Coverage of Cote d'Ivoire
a5572.speech: Indicated that the LOX project will improve the availability of medical oxygen in Cote d'Ivoire, and above all in its most remote regions; according to him, more than 6.5 million US dollars, roughly 4 billion FCFA, were mobilised for the project, which includes training health personnel in the use of the devices as well as the establishment of maintenance and continuous supply procedures ; "By improving access to medical oxygen, we will be able to significantly reduce the mortality rate linked to respiratory diseases, keep our emergency services running and improve the quality of health care, thereby helping to save many lives. We realised that during the Covid period it was oxygen therapy that enabled Cote d'Ivoire to have one of the lowest fatality rates. It is therefore important that we bring pure, quality oxygen to the heart of the regional centres of health excellence." ; according to him, thanks to this investment nearly 30% of all hospitals in Cote d'Ivoire are directly or indirectly covered by these medical liquid oxygen systems, corresponding to a capacity to intervene for more than 60% of the Ivorian population, and he intends to go further to cover the entire national territory.

a5572.speaker: Jessica Davis Ba, United States Ambassador to Cote d'Ivoire
a5572.speech: Said the completion of the LOX project is a strong action by the American people on behalf of the Ivorian people, through USAID; she added that it reflects the good health of bilateral relations between her country and Cote d'Ivoire, at which she expressed her delight.

a5649.speaker: World Food Programme (latest projections)
a5649.speech: According to the latest projections of the World Food Programme, 52 million people will be threatened with acute food insecurity in West and Central Africa during the 2025 lean season.

a5649.speaker: Sahel Adaptive Social Protection Program (SASPP)
a5649.speech: Recommends social safety nets adapted to climate shocks, which are almost non-existent in rural areas of the Sahel.

a5649.speaker: Aïssa Garba, president of a women farmers’ group, on the community radio station in Téra, western Niger
a5649.speech: Warns: “People talk about security, but we forget that the real insecurity here is no longer knowing whether we will eat tomorrow. It is our children who are leaving, for lack of land, for lack of water. If we are helped to keep our fields alive, we will hold on to the rest.”

a5649.speaker: Experts
a5649.speech: From Lake Chad to the Horn of Africa, experts observe the same mechanism: climate change aggravates the vulnerability of societies, destroys local economies and facilitates the entrenchment of armed actors who present themselves as protectors or employers.

a5945.speaker: Michael Kofi Andoh, acting Commissioner of Insurance at the National Insurance Commission (NIC)
a5945.speech: Said the commissioner in his bid to promote the growth and development of the industry was currently working with some partners on various projects; said the NIC, in partnership with FSD Africa, had implemented a regulatory sandbox regime to attract, incubate and test innovative solutions to some of the challenges that hindered the development of the industry ; “The NIC is also partnering with the USAID and the ILO to implement an agricultural insurance fund to facilitate the delivery of suitable and affordable agricultural insurance products for both small and large scale farmers.” ; said a big potential for the growth of the industry lay in reaching out to the micro, small and medium enterprises which were largely excluded from the insurance market, and that the NIC had partnered with the UNDP to develop a “new inclusive insurance strategy to reach out to this all-important segment”.

a5945.speaker: Monica Amissah, acting Managing Director of Ghana Reinsurance Plc
a5945.speech: Said the event was more than an award ceremony, it was a celebration of the partnerships that had been the cornerstone of our success: “Over the years, you are respected cedants - have played a pivotal role in driving the growth of Ghana Reinsurance Plc thereby contributing to the advancement of the entire insurance industry. Your dedication, ingenuity and steadfast support have enabled us to reach significant milestones and created a stronger foundation for the future.”

a5945.speaker: Joseph Adom, Deputy Managing Director (Finance and Administration) of Ghana Reinsurance
a5945.speech: In a welcome address, commended Mr Andoh's remarkable contributions to the country's insurance landscape: “With over two decades of service at the NIC, within which he served as head of supervision and deputy commissioner, he has been a pivotal force in advancing industry regulation and fostering inclusivity.”

a6058.speaker: Authority for the Regulation and Control of Strategic Mineral Substances’ Markets (ARECOMS) (statement)
a6058.speech: said in a statement that the ban will be in place for at least four months ; said the ban is for all cobalt produced in the country, including by small scale or artisanal miners.

a6058.speaker: Patrick Luabeya, ARECOMS President
a6058.speech: “This measure is intended to regulate supply on the international market, which is faced with a production glut,” said in the statement ; he said the export ban of cobalt is effective from February 22 and could either be adjusted or terminated after three months.

a6058.speaker: ARECOMS decree (seen by Reuters), signed by Patrick Luabeya and co-signed by Mines Minister Kizito Pakabomba
a6058.speech: issued to enforce and ensure that mining companies comply with the ban.

a6058.speaker: Democratic Republic of Congo (government)
a6058.speech: said on Monday it has temporarily halted cobalt exports amid a production glut.

a6058.speaker: Bloomberg News
a6058.speech: earlier reported news of the temporary metal exports ban.

a6058.speaker: CMOC Group
a6058.speech: did not immediately respond to emailed questions.

a6058.speaker: Eurasian Resources Group
a6058.speech: did not immediately respond to emailed questions.

a6319.speaker: Fastjet Zimbabwe delayed 2023 annual report
a6319.speech: The company's latest annual report shows that stiffer competition from new entrants in the local aviation space adversely impacted Fastjet Zimbabwe's top line, subsequently plunging it into a US$4 million loss in 2023; according to the report, revenue rose marginally by 1,8 percent to US$50,9 million in 2023 from US$50 million.

a6335.speaker: Albert Einstein (quoted)
a6335.speech: “Madness is doing the same thing over and over and expecting a different result.”

a6335.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6335.speech: Announced the abrupt withdrawal of programmes such as USAID, which has shaken key ecosystems; in Kenya, Ghana and Nigeria USAID programmes are undergoing cuts of 23% to 79%.

a6335.speaker: Gates Foundation
a6335.speech: Announced 200 billion USD mostly directed towards Africa by 2045.

a6335.speaker: The Big Deal (data provider)
a6335.speech: According to The Big Deal, VC fundraising reached the one-billion-USD threshold in the first five months of 2025, against 750 million USD for the same period in 2024.

a6335.speaker: Investment and Development Bank of the Alliance of Sahel States
a6335.speech: Announced as a new sovereign initiative, endowed with 500 billion FCFA, which aims to finance structural projects and create jobs.

a6335.speaker: World Bank
a6335.speech: According to the World Bank, in 2024 teams with at least one female founder captured only 6.8% of VC financing in Africa, and all-female teams around 3% over the 2013-2021 period.

a6335.speaker: Global Entrepreneurship Monitor
a6335.speech: According to the Global Entrepreneurship Monitor, sub-Saharan Africa is the region of the world with the highest rates of women entrepreneurs, around 20-26% depending on the country and the year.

a6335.speaker: GSMA
a6335.speech: According to the GSMA, in 2024 global mobile money reached 1,680 billion dollars in transactions, of which sub-Saharan Africa concentrates about 70% of key uses (bill payments, remittances, merchant payments).

a6422.speaker: U.S. Senator John "Jack" Reed and U.S. Representative Gabriel Felix Kofi Amo
a6422.speech: Have emphasized the importance of sustained investment in Liberia's Education Sector, and made a firm commitment to advocate for continued support to the country's Education Sector during a one-day visit to the Ministry of Education to assess the impact of USAID's support; they expressed their desire to learn as much as possible about the impacts of the recent cuts, while also hearing directly from local leaders about areas of progress.

a6422.speaker: Nekpeh Forkpa, Deputy Education Minister for Administration of Liberia
a6422.speech: Thanked the U.S. government for its longstanding support to Liberia's Education Sector and highlighted the critical role USAID has played in strengthening Liberia's education system, particularly through teacher training programs and institutional capacity building: "USAID's support enabled thousands of students to pursue education locally and abroad, while also helping to establish systems for data collection and analysis that inform national education policy" ; noted that the recent adjustments to USAID programming have forced Liberia to make internal shifts, including reallocating resources and assuming direct responsibility for initiatives such as school feeding.

a6449.speaker: Hans Neumann, dean of the diplomatic corps in Benin (German ambassador)
a6449.speech: “I would like to give a commendation to Beninese democracy, which showed maturity during the organisation of the marches of last 10 December, in which the whole political class behaved well” ; indicated that 2015 will be decisive for the country, which will have to meet the challenge of organising legislative and municipal elections: “A living and stable democracy is a guarantee for development and peace” ; mentioned the government's concern to lead Benin towards progress, modernity and shared prosperity, on the basis of tolerance and permanent dialogue with all the vital forces ; “We encourage you to continue the dialogue with the political class, and the political class to play its part in preserving peace”, reiterating the commitment of the country's technical and financial partners to continue their friendship and cooperation with the country.

a6449.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a6449.speech: “I would like here to reassure once again all the Beninese people and the international community that my government will take all the necessary measures for the proper conduct of the next elections” ; indicated that in terms of financing, his government has honoured all its commitments towards the various bodies in charge of organising the elections.

a6449.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a6449.speech: On regional questions, said Benin has always reaffirmed its attachment to the ties of brotherhood and cooperation with its immediate neighbours and the sub-region, the joint Benin-Niger Council of Ministers of 12 January responding to that logic ; acknowledged the past year was difficult for the states of the region but specified that his government pursued its development programme at a more sustained pace, with the option of promoting public-private partnership, the June 2014 Paris Round Table having enabled the country to mobilise 12 billion dollars ; welcomed Benin's eligibility for the second Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) Compact and Canada's reinstatement of the country on its list of aid concentration countries ; “On the economic front, all indicators are green, with a growth rate of 5.7% in 2014. Benin is one of the three countries in the zone to comply with all the convergence criteria within WAEMU.”

a6449.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a6449.speech: Returned to the Ebola epidemic in Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia, welcoming the appreciable assistance of partners which today allows the situation in the affected areas to be brought under control ; deplored that the African continent is still confronted with conflict situations, notably in Libya, the Central African Republic, eastern DRC, Sudan and Somalia: “Benin joins the member states of the African Union in calling for a rapid operationalisation of the African Capacity for Immediate Response to Crises, pending the complete establishment of the African Standby Force and its Rapid Deployment Capability” ; on the regional strategy against Boko Haram, “This is a worrying situation which today calls upon the entire international community in its fight against terrorism”, affirming his country's commitment to send troops alongside neighbouring countries.

a6458.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China (congratulatory message read by Foreign Minister Wang Yi)
a6458.speech: Xi's congratulatory message was read by China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi at the opening ceremony of the Wednesday event in front of more than 100 ministerial-level officials from FOCAC member states.

a6458.speaker: Wang Yi, China's Foreign Minister
a6458.speech: Put forward five proposals on promoting high-quality China-Africa cooperation, noting that China and Africa need to support each other and uphold the solidarity of the Global South; that China and Africa need to open up to the world and champion international free trade; that China and Africa need to pursue mutual benefit and engage in cooperation on global development; that China and Africa need to uphold justice and defend an equitable international order; and that China and Africa need to carry out exchange and mutual learning and promote diversity of civilizations in the world.

a6458.speaker: Lin Jian, spokesperson for China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a6458.speech: Said President Xi announced that China will implement the policy of granting 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with China zero-tariff treatment for 100 percent tariff lines, provide more facilitation to least developed countries in Africa for their export to China, and work with Africa to further implement the 10 partnership actions, providing important guidance for China and Africa jointly advancing modernization and building an inclusive China-Africa community with a shared future for the new era.

a6458.speaker: Lin Jian, spokesperson for China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a6458.speech: Further noted that over recent years China-Africa relations have achieved great leaps forward; that China and all African countries having diplomatic ties with China have established strategic partnerships and China has been the largest trading partner for Africa for 16 years in a row; that since the FOCAC Beijing Summit last year China has made an additional investment of over RMB 13.3 billion and provided funding of over RMB 150 billion to Africa; and that in the first five months of this year China's imports and exports with Africa reached RMB 963 billion, up by 12.4 percent year-on-year, a record high for the same period.

a6458.speaker: China-Africa Changsha Declaration (adopted by China, 53 African countries and the African Union Commission)
a6458.speech: Declares that the rise and growth of the Global South represents the trend of the times; that the frequent occurrence of unilateralism, protectionism and economic bullying has created severe difficulties for the economic and social development and improvement of livelihood in African countries; and that “Given that certain countries' attempt to disrupt the existing international economic and trade order by tariffs undermines the common good of the international community, we call on all countries, the United States in particular, to return to the right track of resolving trade disputes through consultation based on equality, respect and mutual benefit”, adding that “Development assistance to African countries should be effectively increased, not unilaterally slashed, to provide continued support to help African countries improve people's livelihood, reduce poverty and boost economic and social development” ; it further calls on the international community to uphold true multilateralism, commends China's resolve to defend international equity and justice, commits to the ten partnership actions for modernization, and records China's readiness to expand zero-tariff treatment for 100 percent tariff lines to all 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with China and to deepen cooperation in green industry, e-commerce and e-payment, science and technology, and artificial intelligence.

a6458.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Foreign Minister of Lesotho
a6458.speech: Is leading Lesotho's delegation at the Changsha meeting in China, reinforcing government's steadfast commitment to the principles of the China-Africa Changsha Declaration.

a6466.speaker: Namibia’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations
a6466.speech: Has called for stronger international support to improve access to affordable HIV medicines and ensure sustainable funding for HIV programmes around the world.

a6466.speaker: Johanna Haimene, Oshana Health Director
a6466.speech: Said the region has recorded significant progress in the number of people accessing HIV treatment, whose number currently stands at over 20,000.

a6466.speaker: Dr. Esperance Luvindao, Health and Social Services Minister
a6466.speech: Has announced that Namibia will move towards regulatory approval for the rollout of Lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injection for the treatment and prevention of HIV.

a6466.speaker: Sustjie Mbumba, First Lady of Namibia
a6466.speech: During the opening of the high-level Roundtable Discussion on inequalities, HIV, TB, Malaria, and Pandemics at State House, encouraged individuals and organisations to speak out against inequality or injustice.

a6466.speaker: New health director of the Kavango East Region
a6466.speech: Urges the community to offer love and support to the affected and infected, prompted by high HIV infection and transmission in the region.

a6466.speaker: Ministry of Health and Social Services (MoHSS) Executive Director
a6466.speech: Said HIV prevalence among pregnant women has declined from 22% in 2002 to 14% last year, while welcoming the U.S. Global AIDS Coordinator, Ambassador Dr. John Nkengasong, on a visit to the Katutura State Hospital.

a6466.speaker: Ambassador John Nkengasong, US Global AIDS Coordinator
a6466.speech: Says PEPFAR has invested over N$27 billion in Namibia over the past 18 years.

a6466.speaker: Nicholus Mutenda, Health Control Programme Officer in the Directorate of Special Programmes, Ministry of Health and Social Services
a6466.speech: Says Namibia is doing well in terms of HIV Strategic response.

a6508.speaker: Palestine Monetary Authority
a6508.speech: Released the results of its business cycle index for the current month of February, which showed the continued clear decline in the overall index during the month, against the backdrop of its contraction in both the West Bank and the Gaza Strip alike: the overall index fell to about -12.3 points compared with about -6.1 points in the previous month, and by about 1.0 point compared with February of last year ; the index in the West Bank settled in negative territory for the second consecutive quarter, recording about -5.1 points compared with about -0.4 points the previous month, as a result of declines in the indices of some industrial activities, foremost the construction industries index, affected by the seasonal slowdown in construction, and the fall in the furniture industry index, alongside smaller declines in the leather and traditional industries indices, while increases were limited to the food, plastics and engineering industries ; the deterioration in the Gaza Strip index continued, falling from -21.2 points to about -35.1 points, its lowest level since the Israeli war on the Gaza Strip in the summer of 2014, with a clear decline in the food industry index and falls in the textile and construction industries indices.

a6508.speaker: Owners of industrial establishments in the West Bank
a6508.speech: Reported that production and sales levels declined during the current month relative both to previous levels and to previously expected levels; on the other hand, the level of optimism about the near future remains relatively high among establishment owners, who expressed greater confidence about the level of production and employment over the coming three months.

a6508.speaker: Owners of industrial establishments in the Gaza Strip
a6508.speech: Pointed to a decline in the current volume of orders, which resulted in an accumulation of inventory, along with worsening pessimism about the near future, especially with regard to the level of employment.

a6583.speaker: Scott Perry, US Representative from Pennsylvania (Republican)
a6583.speech: Asserted that Boko Haram is among the terrorist organisations subsidised by the United States' national development agency (USAID), and stressed that the agency reportedly spent 697 million dollars a year, not counting shipments of cash, to finance terrorist organisations including Daesh and ISIS Khorasan as well as their training camps; he made the statement during the inaugural hearing of DOGE (Department of Government Efficiency) on 13 February.

a6689.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a6689.speech: Has appealed to the United Nations General Assembly to support the modalities to actualize the advisory opinion rendered by the International Court of Justice regarding the ongoing conflict in Gaza ; "Prolonged occupation does not justify or make acceptable the hardships and injustices endured. This is particularly true for the people of Gaza, who continue to be brutally massacred. As a country that has endured genocide, Namibia believes that Israel, by intent and by action, is committing genocide. Namibia continues to call for a ceasefire and for humanitarian assistance to flow unhindered into Gaza."

a6689.speaker: International Court of Justice (advisory opinion)
a6689.speech: Stated that Israel's continued occupation of the Gaza Strip and West Bank is a violation of international law; the advisory opinion further outlined that Israel end the war.

a6689.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a6689.speech: Repeated Namibia's call for the lifting of decades' old US blockades against Cuba and Zimbabwe: "Economic hardships continue to affect the sister Republic of Cuba, in stark contrast to the ideals of inclusivity and the goal of leaving no one behind. Namibia calls for the end of the economic, financial, and commercial blockade against Cuba. Namibia also reiterates its call for the immediate and unconditional lifting of illegal sanctions against Zimbabwe, which hinders the country's capacity to achieve Sustainable Development Goals."

a6689.speaker: Nangolo Mbumba, President of Namibia
a6689.speech: Says the world body should help intensify the quest for self-determination for the Sahrawi people, and reminded the Assembly that continued disenfranchisement of the people of Western Sahara is an affront to the UN Charter, its purposes and principles, and that this year's session must change this.

a6744.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States (speech before the Ghanaian Parliament, July 2009)
a6744.speech: the President affirmed that Africa is a fundamental part of our interconnected world, and called for a partnership with Africa “founded on mutual responsibility and mutual respect” ; As President Obama had declared in Ghana, “Africa does not need strongmen, it needs strong institutions.”

a6744.speaker: Barack Obama, President of the United States
a6744.speech: From the moment he took office, President Obama committed himself to supporting stable, open and accountable governments, as well as sustainable development in Africa.

a6744.speaker: US National Security Strategy (published May 2010)
a6744.speech: reinforces this vision and argues in favour of a partnership with African nations as they develop their economies and strengthen their democratic institutions and their governance ; As was mentioned in the National Security Strategy, support for democracy is of capital importance for the interests of the United States and constitutes a fundamental element of American engagement abroad.

a6744.speaker: Presidential Policy Directive approved by President Obama (June 2012)
a6744.speech: In June 2012, the President approved a Presidential Policy Directive which sets out his vision for American policy towards sub-Saharan Africa. The present document draws on that directive and reflects it.

a6744.speaker: United States strategy document on sub-Saharan Africa
a6744.speech: Given the growing strategic importance of sub-Saharan Africa for the United States, over the next five years we will redirect our efforts and multiply them with a view to strengthening democratic institutions and boosting economic growth, trade and investment, while continuing to pursue other objectives on the continent ; the United States has devised a four-pillar strategy as part of its policy towards sub-Saharan Africa: collaborating with the countries of sub-Saharan Africa to strengthen democratic institutions; to stimulate economic growth, trade and investment; to promote peace and security; and to promote opportunity and development.

a6744.speaker: Presidential Directive on Global Development
a6744.speech: The present administration, by means of the Presidential Directive on Global Development, has developed a new approach which emphasises sustainable development, as well as a new operating model for American development assistance which builds on current achievements.

a6819.speaker: Johannes Mururani, participant in the USAID Reach Namibia Project male engagement programme
a6819.speech: told the group he was a violent man until he attended a male engagement programme on gender norms under the USAID Reach Namibia Project. He is now adamant about creating a safe environment. “Imagine a world where boys and girls can walk safely to school without fear of violence. A world where women can make decisions about their health and bodies without coercion. A world where men and women stand together as equals, united in the fight against gender-based violence and HIV.”

a6819.speaker: Katamba Nanyemba, project coordinator of the Reach Namibia Project
a6819.speech: According to Katamba Nanyemba, there is ample evidence linking gender-based violence and HIV. “It shows us that survivors of violence have often limited control over their sexual health, face power imbalances that prevent them from negotiating safer sex, and fear stigma that deters them from accessing critical services.”

a6819.speaker: Bonifatius Wakudumo, Kavango East Governor
a6819.speech: told the group that it is their duty as men to educate themselves and others about GBV, its root causes, and its impact on individuals. “It is believed that five in six men are not abusers. But where are they? Can they stand up and be counted? Can the one in six who are abusers change their ways? Can we raise a new generation based on equality? Change is not easy, and it does not happen overnight. But every step we take today is a step toward building a safer and more equitable future. Let us be unwavering in our commitment and courageous in our actions.”

a6860.speaker: SwissAid report
a6860.speech: Alleged that some gold from South Sudan, Ethiopia, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and possibly Sudan passes through Kenya before being re-exported to Dubai, where it is finally declared for import; reveals that over the past decade Kenya has grown into a popular smuggling hub for gold, primarily destined for the UAE, and that illicit gold outflows from Kenya likely exceed two tons per year while declared gold exports were only 672 kilograms in 2023, the vast majority of gold entering the country leaving without being officially declared for export. The report partly stated: “Part of the gold that is smuggled out of South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and, to a lesser extent, Ethiopia, and possibly Sudan, passes through Kenya before being re-exported. Most of the gold smuggled out of Kenya is shipped to Dubai and declared for import there.” SwissAid further stated that, based on interviews with industry experts and government records, declared gold exports from Kenya often exceed the country’s known gold production and declared imports, leading the NGO to conclude that inbound illicit gold flows are occurring; the report also highlights that the two licensed medium-scale mines responsible for Kenya’s declared gold production export their material to refiners located in South Africa and Switzerland.

a6860.speaker: Government of Kenya
a6860.speech: In response to growing gold smuggling concerns, Kenya is planning to establish a Mining Police Unit and is advocating for regional certification of gems.

a6860.speaker: Ministry of Mining of South Sudan
a6860.speech: Called for an urgent crackdown on rampant gold smuggling at Juba International Airport, describing the illicit trade as a “major challenge” to the nation.

a6860.speaker: Matiok Santino Akuei, Undersecretary in the Ministry of Mining (South Sudan)
a6860.speech: Emphasized the negative impact of the illicit mineral trade on the ministry’s operations. He stated, “The smuggling of gold and precious minerals has become a great challenge for the Republic of South Sudan, undermining our performance.” He urged law enforcement agencies and relevant stakeholders to immediately report any suspicious activities related to mineral smuggling, stressed that the Ministry of Mining holds the sole mandate to license all gold and mineral exports, and warned that any mineral export without proper authorization is illegal and could lead to arrest and prosecution.

a6860.speaker: Bank of South Sudan
a6860.speech: In 2020 announced plans to purchase crude gold locally to boost the economy, focusing on Kapoeta, where thousands of artisanal miners operate.

a6878.speaker: Said Nour Hassan (Director General of CRIPEN), Ayan Osman (executive secretary for education), Mouna Ismail (inspector general of general education), Laura Dillon-Binkley (head of the PED project) and PED officials
a6878.speech: all took part in the closing ceremony of the training and each expressed their enthusiasm about the creation of such a programme, which will be able to make it easier for young people to choose their stream and which will consequently determine their career choice.

a6878.speaker: PED (USAID-funded Djiboutian Workforce Employability Project)
a6878.speech: The curriculum drafting commission will receive support for the development of the occupation-discovery module so that they can be equipped through the integration of some activities of our modules into this programme. The contribution is invaluable because our modules focus on development and interpersonal communication, leadership and introduction to the world of work, etc. All this will guide young people towards a better knowledge of themselves and of their skills from the 6th grade onwards, so that they will be ready to face the world and to better understand their occupations of tomorrow.

a6878.speaker: Ahmed Moussa Ahmed, specialist in formal education at PED
a6878.speech: said the objective of this training of trainers was to introduce the core employability and entrepreneurship skills programme and the work-based learning programme to curriculum designers and pedagogical advisers for the new programme on the discovery of occupations intended for middle-school pupils in general education; said that among the beneficiaries a drafting committee will sit to reflect on the modules and activities to be used in order to produce a programme on the discovery of occupations, a new programme that MENFOP wishes to put in place from the sixth grade; said that during the training the beneficiaries acquired the participatory approaches of training, were led to carry out practical cases of informational interviews with companies near CRIPEN and were able to practise behavioural activities.

a7248.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture, Water, and Land Reform (notice issued by the Directorate of Veterinary Services)
a7248.speech: Announced the resumption of the importation of poultry meat from South Africa to Namibia.

a7248.speaker: Leaders in the Omaheke Region
a7248.speech: Advised the Ministry of Agriculture, Water, and Land Reform to revise the resettlement qualifying criteria in the Resettlement Policy, taking the view that the criteria fall short of addressing the pressing need for resettlement for agricultural purposes.

a7255.speaker: Sakphouseth Meng, Representative and Country Director of the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)
a7255.speech: Said agriculture is an important sector for Tanzania's economy, contributing 29.1 percent of the national GDP while employing more than 65 percent of all people, and that they are meeting with the aim of transforming the country's food systems, from food production and distribution to protecting the environment and tackling challenges such as malnutrition and climate change ; "Agriculture is still an important sector for Tanzania's economy, so its transformation is important for the growth of agriculture and for the welfare and prosperity of all Tanzanians. And since 2021 Tanzania has been drawing on various international efforts to reform its food systems," ; "This transformation requires investment in climate-smart agriculture. The transformation of food systems requires cooperation and strategic investment from all stakeholders."

a7255.speaker: Sakphouseth Meng, Representative and Country Director of the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)
a7255.speech: Said the programme for developing sustainable food systems, implemented by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) and IFAD, is aimed at helping to strengthen Tanzania's food systems and to attract investment.

a7255.speaker: Abdul Mhinte, Deputy Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries
a7255.speech: Said there are two projects funded by various stakeholders, including IFAD, costing more than 200 million US dollars, and that those two five-year projects, implemented in the country starting in 2025, deal with dairy and fisheries ; "The goal of these two projects is to boost production and to look at the entire systems of food production in those areas, from how it is produced until it reaches the consumer, especially taking into account climate change."

a7255.speaker: Abdul Mhinte, Deputy Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries
a7255.speech: Said Tanzania is self-sufficient in food, despite some households, especially rural ones, not being so for various reasons, and that projects such as these help improve food systems so that food reaches consumers with the required quality and delivers the intended nutrition for human health.

a7255.speaker: Margaret Natai, Principal Agriculture Officer, Ministry of Agriculture (representing the national food systems Coordinator)
a7255.speech: Said that as a ministry they are collaborating with other stakeholders in order to implement strategies to ensure sustainable food systems in the country are put into effect, and that in 2021 they drew up goals in various sectors and have guidelines that direct them, including food safety, school feeding for children, food loss and processing ; "Because of that, every stakeholder here has a role to play, and in today's session we are educating stakeholders so that they understand how to organise themselves to reach the goals, including how to use innovative technology in production."

a7255.speaker: Asha Zahran Mohamed, Director of the Livestock Development Department, Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation, Natural Resources and Livestock of Zanzibar
a7255.speech: Said the workshop will help them provide education to citizens on improving food systems and the production of meat and milk.

a7318.speaker: Oluremi Tinubu, First Lady of Nigeria
a7318.speech: Expressed confidence in the country's ability to eliminate tuberculosis (TB) by 2035, highlighting the critical role of partnerships and innovative strategies; speaking at the 2024 National TB Conference in Abuja she commended stakeholders for their dedication but stressed the need for sustained efforts to meet global TB elimination targets ; "Despite progress, Nigeria still has the highest TB burden in Africa and ranks sixth globally.
